title: Memory Access
description:
## Reading and Writing Memory
So far you've only used registers. But registers are limited - there's only 16. Real programs store data in memory.

Brackets `[]` mean "the value AT this address":
```asm
mov al, [myvar]       ; read byte from myvar into al
mov [myvar], byte 42  ; write 42 into myvar
```

You can also use registers as pointers:
```asm
mov rsi, myvar        ; rsi holds the address
mov byte [rsi], 42    ; write 42 to that address
mov al, [rsi]         ; read from that address
```

Or use raw hex addresses directly:
```asm
mov al, [0x402000]    ; read from address 0x402000
mov [0x402000], byte 5 ; write 5 to address 0x402000
```
You can see these addresses in the disassembly tab - that's where your data lives in memory.

- `mov rax, myvar` = put the ADDRESS in rax
- `mov al, [myvar]` = put the VALUE at that address in al

**Use the Step button and check the Registers/Stack tab to watch values move between registers and memory!**

## Assignment:
LHINX stores the boot mode in memory. Read the value from `boot_mode`, compare it to 1. If it equals 1, print `Normal boot`. Otherwise print `Safe mode`.
starterCode:
section .data
    boot_mode db 1
    normal_msg db "Normal boot", 10
    normal_len equ $ - normal_msg
    safe_msg db "Safe mode", 10
    safe_len equ $ - safe_msg

section .text
    global _start

_start:
    ; read boot_mode into al
    ; compare and jump

    mov rax, 60
    xor rdi, rdi
    syscall
